brief: A tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers, with hooks for small hand tools.

requirements.requirement: Rack hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers
requirements.evidence: 5 hex-acc-keyhole accessories, all on the same back slot (5): accessory:0#-1,0#5, 0#0,0#5, 0#1,0#5, 1#-1,0#5, 1#1,0#5. They hang on screws already in the wall. The configurator doesn't check how much load they carry.

6 hex-acc-hook plates (2 hooks each, 12 hooks) on the front slot 2 of every cell, both storeys. A cable coil prop hangs on accessory:1#-1,0#2. The tool props can't be hung on hooks, so I couldn't show actual tools on them.
6 full pieces joined with snaps, joint bolts from lockJoints, and solid caps from capOpenFaces. Mesh check: clear. Strength depends on the print material, which the configurator doesn't check.

finish.summary: I built a wall tool rack: 6 full hex cells, 3 wide and 2 storeys high, with 5 keyhole hangers on the wall side and 6 hook plates (12 hooks) on the front. The configurator check passed with no rule errors and the mesh-collision check came back clear. I closed the open faces with end caps and bolted the joints. The parts list reached 43, a bit over the usual 40-part guide, mostly because I added the second storey. The single-storey version sat so low that a test cable coil hung through the bench, and the second storey also doubles the number of hooks. To show what it's for, I hung a coiled cable on one hook. The tool props can't hang on hooks (hooks only take a cable coil, a roll of gaffer tape or goggles), and gaffer tape hit the walls of the cells next to it. The configurator only checks fit, so I can't vouch for the hooks' strength or how much weight the keyholes can hold.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
